body:
When the shim is installed **as** `gh` on PATH, no real `gh` is ever visible to the PATH scan, so `ResolveGHPath` always falls through to the managed `~/.ghx/bin/gh`. A `brew upgrade gh` then has no effect on what actually runs, and nothing surfaces the discrepancy until the managed copy ages past the 7-day staleness threshold.

This implements suggestions (1) and (3) from the issue: probe the well-known locations a `gh`-named shim shadows, prefer the newer binary, and make other discoverable installs visible in `ghx ghcli status`.

### `src/internal/ghcli/shadow.go` (new)

- `packageManagerGHPaths` — `/opt/homebrew/opt/gh/bin/gh`, `/usr/local/opt/gh/bin/gh`, `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/gh/bin/gh`. These are the real binaries behind the package manager's `bin/gh` symlink, which is what the shim displaces.
- `FindPackageManagerGHs()` — probes them, skipping shims, the managed binary, symlink duplicates, and anything whose `--version` fails.
- `preferNewerGH()` — picks the highest `--version` and prints a one-time stderr notice when a package-manager copy wins.
- `CompareVersions()` — numeric dotted comparison (`2.100.0 > 2.99.0`, pre-release suffixes stripped).

The probe result is cached in `~/.ghx/ghcli-probe.json`, keyed by a fingerprint of each involved binary's path/mtime/size. The steady-state resolve therefore costs zero subprocess executions, and a `brew upgrade gh` invalidates the fingerprint and triggers a fresh probe on the next call.

### `src/internal/ghcli/resolve.go`

`preferNewerGH` is applied to the managed-location branch **and** to the config branch when `gh_path` points at the managed binary — the latter being exactly the reported case (`source: config (gh_path)` → managed).

### `src/cmd/ghx/main.go`

`ghx ghcli status` lists other discoverable binaries and labels the source correctly:

```
gh binary:  /opt/homebrew/opt/gh/bin/gh
source:     package manager (shadowed by the ghx shim)
version:    2.99.0
also found: /Users/x/.ghx/bin/gh (version 2.98.0)
```

The `source` computation previously reported `config (gh_path)` whenever `gh_path` was set, which would now be wrong when the configured path is overridden by a newer discovery; it checks the resolved path instead.

The daemon inherits this via its existing periodic re-resolve from #9.

### Notes for review

- Preference is by version, not by location, so a freshly `ghx ghcli upgrade`d managed binary still wins over an older brew copy.
- The candidate list is empty on Windows; `preferNewerGH` is then a no-op returning the managed path.
- Suggestion (2) from the issue (version-aware staleness against the `cli/cli` release tag) is not included — it adds a network dependency to the resolve path and addresses a different failure mode.

- Fixes #20
title: Prefer newer package-manager gh when the ghx shim shadows it
